question: What are the defaults of rocksdb::ConfigOptions, how is one torn down, and where is the default ctor used?

catalogue.note: byte counts are the repo catalogue's published-crate rebuild comparison; the 22 differing ctor bytes are relocation bytes (the two direct calls), not semantics

fields.name: flag byte 4 (C++ name open)
fields.evidence: movb $0x0,0x4(%rdi) in the ctor; SetOptions sets it to 1

fields.name: delimiter (std::string)
fields.evidence: SSO init in the ctor; Persist replaces it with "\n  ", AsString re-assigns ";"; the inner Persist copies it with the string copy helper

fields.name: u32 field (C++ name open)
fields.evidence: movl $0x0,0x28(%rdi) in the ctor; copied as a u32 by the inner Persist

fields.name: u8 field (C++ name open)
fields.evidence: movb $0xff,0x2c(%rdi) in the ctor; copied as a byte by the inner Persist

fields.name: u64 field (C++ name open)
fields.evidence: movq $0x80000,0x30(%rdi) in the ctor; copied as a qword by the inner Persist; the outer Persist overwrites it with DBOptions+0x220 when that is non-null

fields.name: env (Env*, raw)
fields.evidence: two calls to rocksdb::Env::Default() 0x5fe2860; never released by the dtor

fields.name: registry (std::shared_ptr<ObjectRegistry>)
fields.evidence: NewInstance 0x61f9400 returns by value into +0x40/+0x48; released by the dtor via _M_release on +0x48

steps: store flag bytes 0,1,1,1 at +0x00 and 0 at +0x04
init the delimiter string at +0x08 (SSO, ";", len 1)
call ObjectRegistry::NewInstance() 0x61f9400 with the out-pointer at +0x40
ctor.double_env_call_note: the second Env::Default() call stores the same pointer over the first; no intervening read of +0x38 exists in the ctor, so the first store is dead
ctor.landing_pad: 0x60bb856..0x60bb88a (own FDE): on unwind, releases *(this+0x48) via _M_release and disposes the delimiter string at +0x08, then resumes unwinding

steps: if *(this+0x48) is non-null, _M_release it (the registry shared_ptr control block)
dispose the delimiter string at +0x08 (heap buffer freed only when _M_dataplus != this+0x18)
dtor.note: env at +0x38 is a raw pointer and is not released; the flag bytes and the +0x28/+0x2c/+0x30 scalars need no teardown
dtor.inline_teardown: all nine construction hosts inline this teardown on their normal path (release +0x48, dispose +0x08); D1 is called only from landing pads

new_instance.name: rocksdb::ObjectRegistry::NewInstance()
new_instance.correction: #4015 labelled this routine 'clone'; the catalogue name is NewInstance. It is not a copy: it allocates a fresh 0xd0-byte control block and a fresh 0xc0-byte ObjectRegistry whose parent is the Default singleton
steps: call ObjectRegistry::Default() 0x61f92b0 into a stack temp
operator new(0xd0) for the control block
install control-block vtable 0x64d8f00 (RELATIVE slot 0x64d8f00 -> 0x61f8130), packed counts 0x100000001 from 0x459b20
copy the parent shared_ptr (ptr, cb) into the new registry's parent slot at registry+0x60
zero registry+0x70..+0xb7 (including the mutex slot at +0x98)
release the stack temp's reference to the parent
return the shared_ptr by value (ptr = control block +0x10, cb = control block)
new_instance.resolves: #4015's open unknown: the ObjectRegistry +0x70..0x98 region is zero at construction (NewInstance zeroes registry+0x70..+0xb7); the parent shared_ptr lives at registry+0x60, already pinned by #4015
new_instance.sole_caller: the ConfigOptions ctor at 0x60bb8f0 is the only direct caller binary-wide

sites.consumer_note: copies the incoming CFOptions (0x60c3e10), builds the Configurable view (0x60881b0), runs ConfigureFromMap 0x6097150 over the map
serializes the result's option map with the type map at 0x6501de0
version-1 arm only (first u32 of the input == 1); parses the stored option string with the type map at 0x6501ce0
runs the RegisterEncryptionBuiltins pthread_once (callable 0x5ff9c50) then creates the BlockCipher from the name string through the registry
parses the string map into the out MutableDBOptions with the type map at 0x6506dc0
compares the two MutableDBOptions under the name "MutableDBOptions" (rodata 0x4541e0, 16 bytes)
the inner overload re-copies the ConfigOptions field-by-field (see persist-copy excerpt) and re-applies the "\n  " delimiter

sites.gate: constructs only when the table has a stored prefix-extractor name (*(r12+0x1e0) != 0) and no instantiated transform (*(r13+0x1b0) == 0)
sites.consumer_note: instantiates the table's prefix extractor by name through the registry
the delimiter re-assignment is a no-op: the value written (";") equals the ctor default

dtor_callers.claim: every direct call site of D1 sits inside a landing-pad FDE; no main-path caller exists

glob_dat.note: use-count selector byte read by every shared_ptr release in this packet

data_literals.note: packed (use, weak) counts for make_shared blocks

model.checks: defaults, dtor trace, Persist copy, NewInstance parent/zeroed region, per-site overrides, bbtopen gate

corrections: #4015 called 0x61f9400 'clone'; it is ObjectRegistry::NewInstance() per the catalogue, creating a fresh child registry parented at the Default singleton
#3950 described 0x5fe2860 as 'the default holder initializer'; it is rocksdb::Env::Default() per the catalogue (the holder initialization lives inside it); it has 17 callers binary-wide
open_unknowns: C++ names of the five flag bytes at +0x00..+0x04 (defaults 0,1,1,1,0; Read sets +0x00=1 and +0x03=0, Write and Persist set +0x03=0, SetOptions sets +0x04=1)
C++ names of the scalars at +0x28 (u32, 0), +0x2c (u8, 0xff) and +0x30 (u64, 0x80000)
identity of DBOptions+0x220, the value the outer Persist copies into +0x30 when non-null
C++ name of the SetOptions apply helper 0x60c4550 (no catalogue label): it copies CFOptions, builds the Configurable view and runs ConfigureFromMap 0x6097150
exact argument mapping of the SliceTransform create host 0x61ca3d0 at the BlockBasedTable::Open site (the ConfigOptions is the 2nd argument; the host itself is pinned by #3764)
